reason: A docx whose w:spacing carries a w:lineRule outside auto, exact and atLeast: the TypeScript docx engine keeps the text and converts the document; the Rust docx engine's model refuses the value (invalid value: string aut, expected a string of LineSpacing.rule) and with it the whole docxToOdt. A defect of the Rust docx engine (crates/docx-engine model wire), reported to the docx stream; the odt engine is not involved. Two mutated docx of comparison (c+) show it.

A numeric character reference to a surrogate code point that does not pair with the next reference: the TypeScript writes a lone surrogate into the text, which is not a valid string and loses the character; a Rust string cannot hold one and writes U+FFFD. Adjacent high and low references decode to one character on both sides. TypeScript defect (TS-DEFECTS.md row 4).

An offset argument between the two halves of a surrogate pair: the TypeScript cuts the pair and keeps a lone half; a Rust byte offset cannot point inside a character, so the Rust reads from the end of it. No caller of the engine passes such an offset: every one is a tag boundary. TypeScript defect (TS-DEFECTS.md row 23).
